assessments.summary: The audit establishes both components of the claim. For every deterministic finite-block private-message code, the conditional-mutual-information sum telescopes exactly, Fano bounds its endpoints, time sharing yields the stated approximate dependence balance, memorylessness and deterministic encoding give the fixed-coordinate induced-law factorization, and chain-rule/Csiszar identities prove all four rate rows. For the specified entropy-only BSSC relaxation, the sharp scalar support inequalities are verified and an actual finite entropic witness satisfies the complete listed constraints while attaining both sum branches at 2h_2(1/4)-5/4. Because the witness is genuinely entropic, universally valid finite-variable information inequalities cannot remove it; conditional resampling preserves it through every finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions.
scopeQualifications: The code result assumes a finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast channel, deterministic encoding, independent uniform private messages, and message sizes N_j>=2 with R_j=(1/n)log_2 N_j.
The induced auxiliaries and W may have alphabets growing with blocklength, so the result is not by itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region.
The no-go conclusion applies only to the stated coarse entropy/copy relaxation and finite sequences of standard copy-lemma extensions.
The finite witness is deliberately not a binary-input BSSC law: X is tuple-valued. Exact binary-posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints can exclude it and remain viable.
The theorem does not establish a new capacity upper bound.
